A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffCLF research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, molecular simulations, compositional sampling, Boltzmann-generator evaluations and free-energy estimates.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative molecular results for DiffCLF in Table 11. That table explicitly attributes its DSM and FPE comparator results to Plainer et al.

M1.justification: The defining objectives and method extensions remain unchanged. However, new Algorithms 1–2 conflict with Equations (10) and (12): the binary softplus signs are reversed, and Algorithm 2 minimizes class probability without the negative logarithm. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are documentation errors or procedural revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MOG-2/MOG-40, OR/AND composition, Müller-Brown, alanine dipeptide, Chignolin and implicit-solvent/vacuum free-energy estimation. The newly specified coarse-graining details do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds DSM-plus-FPE as a quantitative comparator for ALDP and Chignolin, using results attributed to Plainer et al. v1's molecular comparison used DSM alone; its discussion and property table mentioning FPE were not empirical comparisons. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The molecular results paragraph changes the reported classification count from N=4 to N=2, although v3 Figure 9 still specifies four classes. Table 11 introduces JS divergence, PMF error and training-time evaluation. Existing Gaussian-mixture training and evaluation settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish which molecular experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The classification-level sweeps and stochastic-interpolant log-density diagnostics are retained. The added molecular benchmark scores do not introduce a distinct ablation, sensitivity, robustness or distribution-shift analysis.

E5.justification: Table 11 newly specifies molecular results as mean ± standard deviation over three random seeds. The Gaussian-mixture experiments retain their two-seed reporting. This establishes additional uncertainty reporting, not an explicit increase in molecular run counts.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1, 2 and 4–10 are unchanged. New Table 11 supplies molecular accuracy and timing results: Chignolin Langevin JS is 0.0181 for DiffCLF versus 0.0050 for FPE, with estimated training times of 18.9 versus 49.6 GPU hours. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4.2 adds local O(delta²) weak-approximation bounds and regularity conditions. Appendix D.5 expands the Jacobian and Taylor reasoning, revises remainder terms and the Gaussian normalization constant, and corrects the concluding limit from delta tending to infinity to zero. The central uniqueness and consistency results are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims and the four stated contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion replaces the characterization of DiffCLF as an 'unbiased' training principle with 'consistent', a limited revision of its statistical claim.

C2.justification: New Remark 2.1 explains why strict normalization is unnecessary for the listed downstream applications. The molecular discussion adds an interpretation of FPE-comparable quality with 1.5–2.5× faster training, although Table 11 shows larger Chignolin errors. The explicit limitation concerning access to Chignolin ground-truth data is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code location, binary and multiclass training pseudocode, explicit preconditioning and network parameterization, coarse-graining dimensions, and A100 timing-estimation details. It removes v1's disclosure of using 50,000 generated Chignolin samples. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation, though the new pseudocode conflicts with the stated objectives.

R1.justification: v3 adds empirical efficiency positioning against Plainer et al.'s FPE method and changes the attribution of joint DSM/time-score training from Yu et al. to Guth et al. Most bibliography changes are publication updates; the He-to-Du citation change still identifies the same FEAT work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations, an Impact Statement, a descriptive appendix outline replacing the contents list, new appendix subdivisions, and author/header and cross-reference edits.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. v1's connections diagram, Figure 6, is removed; molecular plots are revised; two training algorithm displays and Table 11 are added. The rearrangement also resolves the figure/caption overlap visible on v1 page 10.

improvement.justification: Table 11 strengthens molecular evaluation, while the revised layout, code location and preconditioning exposition improve usability. However, the new pseudocode contradicts the stated loss, molecular text and captions disagree on class count, and Chignolin data provenance is less explicit. The FPE-comparable-quality interpretation also understates larger Chignolin errors. These benefits and substantive reproducibility and interpretation problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
